fkszph40q7xknINSERT INTO GLBTMPACBK (TDATE, AC_NO, DRCR, CSH_TRN, PRTCLS, DEBIT, CREDIT, BALANCE, DOC_NO, ACMASTCODE, PASS, POST, CTRNNO, OTRNNO, VOU_NO, VOU_SRNO, OP_ID , SU_ID, RC_COUNT, FD_COUNT, CHQ_PREFIX, CASHIER_ID, CASHIER_OK, CASH_CR, CASH_DR, CSHR_EXCP, DENMTION , REF_ACNO, REF_ACMCD , CHQBOUNCE, FORBRANCH, ATBRANCH, VOU_GRNO , DD_GRNO, GOLD_REC_NO, DD_CLEAR, INTFRDT, INTTODT, AC_TYPE, RECEIPTNO, FD_RC_CNT , SHIFT_NO, PROC_SRNO, AC_CODE, TRNSCNID) SELECT A.TDATE, A.AC_NO, A.DRCR, A.CSH_TRN, A.PRTCLS, A.DEBIT, A.CREDIT, A.BALANCE, A.DOC_NO, A.ACMASTCODE, :"SYS_B_00", A.POST, A.CTRNNO, A.OTRNNO, A.VOU_NO, A.VOU_SRNO, A.OP_ID , A.SU_ID, A.RC_COUNT, A.FD_COUNT, A.CHQ_PREFIX, A.CASHIER_ID, A.CASHIER_OK, A.CASH_CR, A.CASH_DR, A.CSHR_EXCP, A.DENMTION , A.REF_ACNO, A.REF_ACMCD , A.CHQBOUNCE, A.FORBRANCH, A.ATBRANCH, A.VOU_GRNO , A.DD_GRNO, A.GOLD_REC_NO, A.DD_CLEAR, A.INTFRDT, A.INTTODT, A.AC_TYPE, A.RECEIPTNO, A.FD_RC_CNT , A.SHIFT_NO, A.PROC_SRNO, B.AC_CODE, A.TRNSCNID FROM ACBK A, ACMAST B WHERE A.ACMASTCODE=B.ACMASTCODE AND A.TDATE = :"SYS_B_01" AND ATBRANCH = :"SYS_B_02" AND NVL(A.CNCLED, :"SYS_B_03") !=:"SYS_B_04" AND A.TRN_TYPE = :"SYS_B_05" AND A.CSH_TRN!= :"SYS_B_06" AND NVL(A.SSD_QUICK, :"SYS_B_07")=:"SYS_B_08" AND NVL(A.SRCOFTRN, :"SYS_B_09") NOT IN (:"SYS_B_10", :"SYS_B_11", :"SYS_B_12") AND NVL(A.POST, :"SYS_B_13")<>:"SYS_B_14" ORDER BY VOU_GRNO, OTRNNO

          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 1.33 active sessions, 18.18% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.33 active sessions, 18.18% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 2: Soft Parse
Impact is .94 active sessions, 12.88% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .94 active sessions, 12.88% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .94 active sessions, 12.88% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "1000" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 3: "User I/O" wait Class
Impact is .73 active sessions, 10.05% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
Wait class "User I/O" was consuming significant database time.
Waits for I/O to temporary tablespaces were not consuming significant database
time.
The throughput of the I/O subsystem was not significantly lower than expected.

   No recommendations are available.

Finding 5: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .48 active sessions, 6.53% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .48 active sessions, 6.53% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .76 active sessions, 10.36% of total activity.


Finding 6: Undersized SGA
Impact is .42 active sessions, 5.81% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
The SGA was inadequately sized, causing additional I/O or hard parses.
The value of parameter "sga_target" was "143360 M" during the analysis period.

   Recommendation 1: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .11 active sessions, 1.51% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Increase the size of the SGA by setting the parameter "sga_target" to
      152320 M.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .76 active sessions, 10.36% of total activity.
      Wait class "User I/O" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .73 active sessions, 10.05% of total activity.


Finding 7: Commits and Rollbacks
Impact is .27 active sessions, 3.74% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Waits on event "log file sync" while performing COMMIT and ROLLBACK operations
were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Host Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .27 active sessions, 3.74% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the possibility of improving the performance of I/O to the
      online redo log files.
   Rationale
      The average size of writes to the online redo log files was 28 K and the
      average time per write was 0 milliseconds.
   Rationale
      The total I/O throughput on redo log files was 10 M per second for reads
      and 19 M per second for writes.
   Rationale
      The redo log I/O throughput was divided as follows: 0% by RMAN and
      recovery, 65% by Log Writer, 0% by Archiver, 0% by Streams AQ and 34% by
      all other activity.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Commit" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .27 active sessions, 3.74% of total activity.


Finding 8: Java Execution
Impact is .17 active sessions, 2.27% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
JAVA execution consumed significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .17 active sessions, 2.27% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Look at the "Top SQL Statements" finding for SQL statements consuming

Finding 9: Hard Parse Due to Sharing Criteria
Impact is .17 active sessions, 2.26% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements with the same text were not shared because of cursor
environment mismatch. This resulted in additional hard parses which were
consuming significant database time.
Common causes of environment mismatch are session NLS settings, SQL trace
settings and optimizer parameters.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .17 active sessions, 2.26% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Look for top reason for cursor environment mismatch in
      V$SQL_SHARED_CURSOR.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .76 active sessions, 10.36% of total activity.
